H11-pos1.label: violation
H11-pos1.note: The domain's RETRY_NEXT_DAY table is keyed by the carrier's reject codes (RJ_...), FreightRefusedError carries the raw carrier code, and the book-freight use case looks it up.

H11-pos2.label: violation
H11-pos2.note: FreightRefusedError carries the carrier's raw reject code, and the book-freight use case retries the next day when it equals the vendor code RJ_NO_COLLECTION_SLOT.

H11-twin1.label: clean
H11-twin1.note: Same next-day retry as H11-pos2, but the use case checks the nursery's own refusal value no-slot; the vendor code stays in the gateway's translation.

H11-legit1.label: clean
H11-legit1.note: The nursery adds its own 900 kg load rule and an OverweightLoadError, declared in the glossary; the word overweight also appears in the carrier's code RJ_OVERWEIGHT.

H11-pos3.label: violation
H11-pos3.note: The domain's dispatch manifest names its columns with an array of the carrier's field names (consignment_no, consignee_postcode, pallet_count, gross_weight_kg).

H11-pos4.label: violation
H11-pos4.note: The application layer holds FREIGHT_FIELDS, a table from the core request fields to the carrier's field names; the gateway builds the vendor request from it.

H11-twin2.label: clean
H11-twin2.note: Same FREIGHT_FIELDS table as H11-pos4, in adapters/out/freight/freight-fields.ts; the vendor field names stay in the adapter.

H11-pos5.label: violation
H11-pos5.note: The webhook passes the carrier's raw status into the command, and the record-delivery use case compares it with the vendor literal OUT_FOR_DELIVERY to mark the order shipped.

H11-twin3.label: clean
H11-twin3.note: Same feature as H11-pos5, but the webhook maps OUT_FOR_DELIVERY to the nursery's own outcome on-van and the use case checks that.

H11-SEM-pos1.label: violation
H11-SEM-pos1.note: DeliveryStage renames the carrier's six consignment statuses one to one (the webhook maps each to one); DispatchOrder.track in src/domain/dispatch-order.ts branches on it.

H11-SEM-twin1.label: clean
H11-SEM-twin1.note: The nursery adds an awaiting outcome; the webhook folds the carrier's six statuses into four core outcomes (COLLECTED, AT_HUB and OUT_FOR_DELIVERY all become in-transit).

H03-pos1.label: violation
H03-pos1.note: The webhook (driving adapter) imports parseCarrierDate from the outbound freight adapter package adapters/out/freight: inbound adapter to outbound adapter.

H03-twin1.label: clean
H03-twin1.note: Same date helper as H03-pos1, placed in the driving side's shared folder adapters/in/shared and used by the webhook and the HTTP controller.

H03-twin2.label: clean
H03-twin2.note: The freight gateway and the email notifier both import withRetry from the driven-side shared helper adapters/out/shared.

H07-pos1.label: violation
H07-pos1.note: The new cancel-dispatch use case returns HTTP status numbers (404, 409, 204) as its result, and the controller copies result.status into the reply.

H07-twin1.label: clean
H07-twin1.note: Same cancel feature as H07-pos1; the use case returns a business outcome (cancelled, too-late) or throws a domain error, and the HTTP controller chooses 204, 409 or 404.

H07-legit1.label: clean
H07-legit1.note: DispatchOrder gains a field named statusCode that holds the plant health passport status (PP-PENDING, PP-CLEAR, PP-HOLD), a business status declared in the glossary; next to the existing status field.
